Artifact context bundle (version 1, curated lineage):
Repository: temper-benchmark/production-shaped-rust-change

Primary artifact:
- issue #103 — Add configurable delivery-policy severities [open] kind=code labels=code, ready

## Implementation contract
Extend the dependency-free delivery-policy crate with public Severity (Advisory, Required), PolicyOptions, Rule, Violation, expanded Decision, and summary APIs. Preserve parse_policy, evaluate_labels, Decision.accepted, Decision.missing, and render_decision as compatibility surfaces. Compatibility results remain comma-separated required-only behavior and exact short strings `accepted` or `missing: <labels>`. New wrappers must delegate to the richer path.

Parse one rule per physical line as `severity:label`. Ignore blank lines and whole-line `#` comments. Split the first colon; trim fields; lowercase labels; reject missing colon, unknown severity, empty label, and duplicates after normalization. ParsePolicyError carries the one-based physical line and stable safe text. Add parse_policy_with_options.

Normalize observed labels. In prefix mode, normalize and strip the configured prefix before matching; unprefixed observations do not match accidentally. Preserve declaration order in required and advisory violations. Normal mode blocks only on required violations; strict mode also blocks on advisories without moving them between buckets.

Keep render_decision compatible. Add a stable detailed report: decision line, separate required/advisory lines using `none` for empty buckets and comma-space declaration order, then required/advisory/total counts. Expose the same counts as typed values.

Update thin exports, focused parser/evaluator/report tests, one public integration workflow, README compatibility and rich-path examples, and CHANGELOG. Run `cargo fmt` and `cargo test -q`, inspect the complete diff, and call submit_for_pr.

Mandatory lineage (decision-dense projection):
- feature #100 — Configurable delivery policy classification [open] kind=feature labels=feature, planned
  - Why: downstream clients currently reimplement severity, namespace handling, normalization, ordering, and reporting inconsistently.
  - Product boundary: severity is separate from portable label identity; repository namespace is an evaluation option. The crate stays serialization-agnostic and dependency-free.
- plan #101 — Deliver configurable policy parsing, evaluation, and reports [open] kind=plan labels=plan, planned
  - Architecture: model.rs owns public domain values; parser.rs syntax and compatibility adaptation; evaluate.rs matching and decisions; report.rs text projection; lib.rs only declarations/re-exports. Tests follow those responsibilities plus one integration workflow.
  - Risks: compatibility drift, two evaluator paths, unstable diagnostics, wrong prefix-normalization stage. Centralize normalization and delegate compatibility wrappers.
- design note #99 — Delivery labels across repository conventions [closed] kind=design
  - Decisions: preserve declaration order, reject normalized duplicates across severities, and keep prefix processing out of parsing. Existing automation depends on public missing labels and exact short reports.
- research #98 — Stable policy diagnostics and compatibility constraints [closed] kind=design
  - Evidence retained: mixed-case duplicates and whitespace are common; line numbers include ignored lines; errors identify invalid values without echoing the whole policy. Strict mode changes acceptance only, not violation classification. Detailed output is stable text, not serialization.
  - Non-goals: glob/regex matching, serde, filesystem or environment loading, exemptions, branch-aware behavior, automatic migration, sorting, inline comments, dependency or edition changes.

Follow-up instructions:
- Implement a real product diff; do not modify benchmark metadata or add bookkeeping markers.
- Do not commit, push, or open a pull request; the harness owns publication.
- Prefer cohesive mutation batches across implementation, tests, and docs.
- Validate once after the planned implementation; any later mutation requires revalidation.
- Review tracked and untracked deliverables, call submit_for_pr, then emit the WorkspaceResult JSON envelope.
